result.topic_en: Three trigonometric relations expressing cos(T+U), divided by various products of functions of T and U, in terms of cos(T'+U')·cos(T'−U') over functions of T' and U'.
result.transcription:
$\frac{\cos(T+U)}{\cos T\cos U} = \frac{\cos(T'+U').\cos(T'-U')}{\cos T'^2}$
$\frac{\cos(T+U)}{\sin T\sin U} = \frac{\cos(T'+U')\cos(T'-U')}{\sin U'^2}$
$\frac{2\cos(T+U)}{\sqrt{\sin 2T.\sin 2U}} = \frac{\cos(T'+U').\cos(T'-U')}{\cos T'\sin U'}$

methods.what: Relation between cos(T+U)/(cos T cos U) and cos(T'+U')cos(T'−U')/cos²T'
Relation between cos(T+U)/(sin T sin U) and cos(T'+U')cos(T'−U')/sin²U'
Geometric-mean combination of the two preceding relations: 2cos(T+U)/√(sin2T sin2U) = cos(T'+U')cos(T'−U')/(cos T' sin U')
